title: Humanoid Robots Set to Enter Japanese Convenience Stores
key_facts: Humanoid robots for stocking shelves, managing inventory, packing goods and serving customers in more than 20 languages were shown at a retail industry event in Tokyo on 8 Oct 2026.
The event drew participants from 18 countries, mostly in Asia, and more than 30 exhibiting companies.
A central exhibit was the C1, a store humanoid from CP AI Robotics, a company operating mainly in Thailand.
The company says C1 can identify products, manage inventory, carry goods, refill shelves and bag purchases, and talks with shoppers using facial expressions and gestures.
CP AI Robotics plans full-scale deployment of C1 in Japanese convenience stores as early as 2027.
Weidong Sun of CP AI Robotics said labour shortages are serious for Japan's convenience stores and that one or more robots per store could cut workload and improve night-time security.
Sun said: 'We are not aiming for completely unmanned stores.'
Some robots at the show only danced for visitors; the article does not say which tasks were shown live.
quote_evidence: Humanoid robots capable of stocking shelves, managing inventory, packaging products, and serving customers in more than 20 languages were showcased at an international retail industry event in Tokyo on October 8, highlighting the growing potential of artificial intelligence to transform store operations as Japan struggles with chronic labor shortages.

The company plans to begin full-scale deployment of the C1 in Japanese convenience stores as early as 2027, positioning the technology as a potential response to staffing difficulties across the country's retail sector.
"We are not aiming for completely unmanned stores. We believe the human touch is absolutely essential,"
why_it_matters_hint: Japan's convenience stores are short of workers and a robot maker is aiming at them from 2027, though the plan is unproven.
notes: Single outlet; capabilities are the maker's claims, not independent tests. The article gives no job title for Weidong Sun. 2027 deployment is a plan, not a contract; no store chain is named.
